skill.name: sub-agents
skill.desc: Delegating work to sub-agents with thorough, standalone prompts.
skill.overview:
Sub-agents are stateless workers. They read context, execute, report back. You orchestrate - maintaining continuity across their isolated runs.
The key: prompts must stand alone. A sub-agent has no memory of your session. Everything it needs goes in the prompt.
skill.critical:
**No hacks. Fix properly.**
When something is broken or missing, fix it the right way. Never use workarounds, symlinks, or hacks just because a previous session did. If context files describe a hack, that's a problem to fix - not a pattern to follow.
Wrong: - Symlinks instead of proper git submodules - Copying files instead of cloning repos - scp/rsync for source code - "Quick fix" that papers over the real issue - Presenting hacks as "options" alongside proper solutions
Right: - Git repos with proper remotes - Submodules that resolve on all machines - Dependencies managed through package managers or git - Fix the root cause
If something isn't set up properly on a remote machine, the first task is to set it up properly. No exceptions. No "options." There is only one way: the right way.
**Remote code must be in git.**
When dispatching sub-agents to work on remote machines, ensure the code is in a proper git repository. Never instruct sub-agents to use scp/rsync for source files.
If the remote doesn't have a git repo set up, the sub-agent's first task is to clone it properly.
skill.when_to_use:
- Task is bounded and well-defined - Fresh context helps (no accumulated confusion) - Work can be parallelized - Cross-machine operations - You want to preview the full plan before execution
Not for: quick lookups, simple edits, conversational exploration.
skill.prompt_anatomy:
```markdown You are [doing X] for [project].
## Context Files to Read First
[Ordered list of LLXML files - kernel, skills, specs]
## The Task
[Clear description of what to accomplish]
## Key Files
[Specific paths to read/modify, with line numbers if relevant]
## Steps
[Numbered, actionable steps]
## Constraints
[What NOT to do - don't commit, don't push, don't delete, etc.]
## Final Report
[Exact format you expect back] ```
skill.context_files:
Always include relevant context. Common pattern:
```markdown ## Context Files to Read First
1. /path/to/llxml/main/self.xml - LLXML kernel 2. /path/to/llxml/main/skills/[relevant-skill].xml 3. /path/to/project/META/spec/[app].xml - App architecture 4. /path/to/project/META/skills/[project-skill].xml - Project-specific ```
More context = better results. Don't skimp. The sub-agent starts cold.
skill.cross_machine:
For remote work, include network details:
```markdown ## Network
- Machine A: 10.x.x.x (role, OS, capabilities) - Machine B: 10.x.x.x (role, OS, capabilities)
SSH access: \`\`\`bash export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/path/to/agent ssh -A user@host "..." \`\`\` ```
The `-A` flag forwards your SSH agent. Sub-agents need this spelled out.
skill.preview_pattern:
Always preview before firing:
``` Here's the full prompt for the sub-agent:
---
[complete prompt]
---
Ready to fire when you approve. ```
This catches missing context, wrong scope, bad assumptions. User can adjust before execution.

agent_types.implementer: Creates worktree, writes code, runs tests, reports results. Returns: files changed, test results, issues encountered.
agent_types.reviewer: Audits code or tickets against requirements. Returns: APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED with specifics.
agent_types.investigator: Debugs issues, traces code paths, identifies root causes. Returns: root cause, affected files, proposed fix.
agent_types.deployer: Builds, copies binaries, restarts services, verifies health. Returns: version deployed, health check results, any errors.
agent_types.auditor: Checks status of work against tickets/requirements. Returns: status table, actions taken, remaining work.

skill.validation:
Don't blindly trust results. For reviews especially:
1. Sub-agent claims issue at file:line 2. Read that file yourself 3. Verify claim is accurate 4. Apply only valid findings
Expect occasional hallucinated issues. Validate before acting.
skill.orchestration:
You maintain continuity:
1. Assess task, decide sub-agent is appropriate 2. Write thorough prompt with all context 3. Preview with user 4. Fire sub-agent 5. Receive and validate results 6. Apply changes or iterate 7. Move to next task
Sub-agents are your hands. You're the brain.
